(BY SHRI SANTOSH YADAV - DY. GOVT. ADVOCATE &
 SHRI ROOP SINGH MARAVI - ADVOCATE FOR OBJECTOR)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is first application filed by applicant/accused under Section 439 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.544/2023, registered at Police Station- Amarwara District-Chhindwara (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366(ka), 376(2)(n), 343, 368, 506 of IPC & Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
2. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.

No allegations are made against applicant in statement recorded under Neelesh Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177107605/
1 Section 164 of Cr.P.C in Court.

entities.text: Neelesh Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In these circumstances, applicant may be enlarged on bail.

3. Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the State as well as counsel appearing for objector bail application and it is submitted that as per statement given by prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, applicant was along with Nitin Verma and has kidnapped the prosecutrix and,
thereafter, she was subjected to rape.
It is also submitted that there is no allegation of rape against applicant-Neelesh Verma.
He is said to have helped other co-accused persons.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
5.
On perusing statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C in Court, it is found that applicant has not been named as accused and no allegation of rape is made against him.
6. Considering aforesaid circumstances, b ail application filed by the applicant is allowed.

It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
7. Applicant shall abide by the conditions stipulated in Section 437 (3) of Cr. P. C. C.C. as per rules.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE nd Neelesh Verma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177107605/
